title: Evolution of modern man starting from anthropoid ancestor
topicTitle: Evolution of modern man starting from anthropoid ancestor
notes: [Remember] Humans belong to order Primates, family Hominidae; anthropoid ancestors (dryopithecines) gave rise to hominins — humans did not evolve from living apes but share a common ancestor with them.

[Remember] Sequence: Dryopithecus → Australopithecus afarensis ('Lucy', bipedal, ~400 cc brain) → Homo habilis (tool maker, ~650 cc) → Homo erectus (fire, ~900 cc) → Homo sapiens neanderthalensis → Homo sapiens sapiens (~1350 cc).
[Understand] Key trends: habitual bipedalism, brain expansion, face flattening with chin, dental reduction, opposable thumb refinement, and prolonged infant dependency with culture and language.
[Understand] Evidence: fossils (Africa–Asia–Europe), tool industries (Oldowan, Acheulean), anatomically modern humans appearing ~300,000 years ago in Africa and spreading worldwide.
[Apply] Table contrasting Australopithecus vs Homo habilis vs Homo erectus vs modern man (posture, brain size, tools, one example each).
[Analyze/Evaluate] Why bipedalism first: freed hands for tools, energy-efficient travel; brain growth followed tool use and cooking — support with the Lucy-to-sapiens timeline.
[Create] NEB answer frame: position in classification → stage table with brain size → two trends explained → fossil/tool evidence → labelled timeline sketch.
confusion: Humans did not evolve from living apes; both share an extinct common anthropoid ancestor.
Bipedalism came before major brain expansion — Lucy walked upright with a ~400 cc brain.
Homo habilis made tools, Homo erectus used fire; do not merge their achievements.
Neanderthals were a subspecies of Homo sapiens, not a separate failed genus.
practice: Order the six hominin stages with brain size and one trait each.
Draw the Lucy-to-sapiens timeline with posture and tool labels.
Recall card: stage → brain cc → tool → evidence.
universalFacts: Brain size roughly tripled from Australopithecus (~400 cc) to modern man (~1350 cc).
Bipedalism preceded tool culture; tool culture preceded agriculture and writing.
Fossil plus tool-industry evidence together make a complete NEB answer.
examples: Australopithecus afarensis 'Lucy': upright walker, ~400 cc brain, no true tools.
Homo erectus: controlled fire, Acheulean hand axes, ~900 cc brain, first out-of-Africa spread.
Homo sapiens sapiens: ~1350 cc brain, language, art and agriculture.
practiceQuestions: Give the systematic position of man up to family with two characters of each rank. (3)
Describe the stages of human evolution from Australopithecus to modern man. (5)
Explain two major trends of human evolution with fossil evidence. (4)
keyPoints: Fossil and tool evidence plus timeline
summary: Evolution of modern man: anthropoid ancestry, Lucy-to-sapiens stages with brain sizes, bipedalism and brain-expansion trends, fossil and tool evidence, labelled timeline.

mcqs.question: 'Lucy' (Australopithecus afarensis) is famous for:
mcqs.explanation: Lucy walked upright before major brain expansion — bipedalism first.

mcqs.question: Homo erectus is distinguished by:
mcqs.explanation: Homo erectus (~900 cc) controlled fire and spread out of Africa.

mcqs.question: Modern man (Homo sapiens sapiens) has a brain of about:
mcqs.explanation: Brain size roughly tripled from Australopithecus to modern man.
